billion.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New id="ia93b0982ac5a41c886e2ca227f9cc000_34"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Capital Markets</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">At year-end, we had</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">$2.4 billion of immediate liquidity</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> consisting of $978 million of cash and restricted cash and $1.4&#160;billion available on our $2.2 billion revolving credit facilities. Today, we have $2.6 billion of immediate liquidity. We also have approximately $10&#160;billion of unencumbered assets.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Since January 1, 2025, we have</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">executed capital market transactions totaling $5.1&#160;billion</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. Our capital markets team had a strong year.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In January, we repaid our $450 million 3.50% senior unsecured notes on their maturity date.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In April, our Fifth Avenue and Times Square JV completed a $450&#160;million financing of 1535 Broadway. The non-recourse, interest-only loan bears interest at a fixed rate of 6.90% and matures in May 2030. After transaction costs and reserves, $407&#160;million of the net proceeds from the financing were used to partially redeem Vornado&#8217;s preferred equity on the asset.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In June, a joint venture, in which we have a 50.1% interest, completed a $675 million refinancing of Independence Plaza, a 1,328-unit residential complex in the Tribeca submarket of Manhattan. The non-recourse, interest-only loan bears interest at a fixed rate of 5.84% and matures in June 2030. The loan replaced the previous $675 million loan that was scheduled to mature in July 2025 and bore interest at 4.25%.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In July, we completed a $450 million refinancing of PENN 11, a 1,200,000 square foot Manhattan office building. The five-year  interest-only loan matures in August 2030 and has a fixed rate of 6.35%. We paid down by $50&#160;million the prior $500&#160;million loan that bore interest at a rate of SOFR plus 2.06% (swapped to an all-in fixed rate of 6.28%) and was scheduled to mature in October 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In August, we completed a $120 million refinancing of 4 Union Square South, a 204,000 square foot Manhattan retail property. The    ten-year interest-only loan matures in September 2035 and has a fixed rate of 5.64%. The loan replaced the previous $120 million loan that bore interest at SOFR plus 1.50% and was scheduled to mature in August 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In December, Alexander&#8217;s, in which we own a 32.4% common equity interest, completed a $175 million refinancing of Rego Park II shopping center, located in Queens, New York. The five-year interest-only loan matures in December 2030 and bears interest at a rate   of SOFR plus 2.00%. Alexander&#8217;s paid down by $23.5 million&#160;the prior $198.5 million loan that bore interest at a rate of SOFR plus 1.45% that was scheduled to mature in December 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In December, Alexander&#8217;s restructured the $300 million mortgage loan on the retail condominium portion of 731 Lexington Avenue, which previously bore interest at SOFR plus 1.51%. The restructured loan was split into (i) a $132.5&#160;million senior A-Note that was purchased by a wholly owned subsidiary of Alexander&#8217;s, which bears interest at a fixed rate of 7.00% and (ii) a $167.5 million junior    C-Note held by the lenders of the original loan, which accrues PIK interest at 4.55%. In addition, Alexander&#8217;s has the right to fund operating shortfalls, interest on the A-Note and capital for re-leasing at the property through a B-Note, which will be junior to the A-Note and senior to the C-Note. The B-Note bears interest at a fixed rate of 13.50%, except for loan amounts above $65&#160;million used to pay interest on the A-Note, which will bear interest at a fixed rate of 7.00%. The restructured loan matures in December 2035.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In January 2026, a joint venture, in which we have a 50.0% interest, entered into a nine-month extension with the lenders on the $54&#160;million mortgage loan encumbering the office condominium of 825 Seventh Avenue and simultaneously paid down the principal balance by $6&#160;million to $48&#160;million. The loan was previously scheduled to mature in January 2026. The non-recourse, interest-only  loan bears interest at a rate of SOFR plus 2.75% and matures in October 2026, with a fifteen-month extension option subject to         loan-to-value and debt yield requirements.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In January 2026, a joint venture, in which we have a 53.0% interest, completed a $250 million refinancing of 7 West 34th Street, a 477,000 square foot Manhattan office and retail building. The non-recourse, five-year interest-only mortgage loan matures in February 2031 and has a fixed rate of 5.79%. The joint venture paid down by $50 million the prior $300 million full-recourse loan that bore interest at 3.65% and was scheduled to mature in June 2026. The loan was paid down using property-level reserves and a $25 million member loan from Vornado which accrues interest at 16.00% and receives priority on distributions.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">10</font></div></div></div><div id="ia93b0982ac5a41c886e2ca227f9cc000_37"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Capital Markets - continued</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In January 2026, we completed a public offering of $500 million 5.75% senior unsecured notes due February 1, 2033 (&#8220;2033 Notes&#8221;). Interest on the senior unsecured notes is payable semi-annually on February 1 and August 1, commencing August 1, 2026. The 2033&#160;Notes were sold at 99.824% of their face amount to yield 5.78%. A portion of the $494 million net proceeds from the 2033 Notes will be used to repay our $400 million senior unsecured notes due June 2026 at maturity.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In January 2026, we completed a $1.105 billion refinancing of one of our two revolving credit facilities. On February 4, 2026, the facility was upsized to $1.130 billion. The $1.130 billion amended facility currently bears interest at a rate of SOFR plus 1.05% and is scheduled to mature in February 2031 (as fully extended). The facility fee is 25 basis points. The facility replaced the previous $1.25 billion revolving credit facility which was scheduled to mature in December 2027.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In January 2026, we upsized our $915 million revolving credit facility that matures in April 2029 (as fully extended) to $1.0&#160;billion. The credit facility currently bears interest at a rate of SOFR plus 1.16% and has a facility fee of 24 basis points.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In January 2026, we completed a refinancing of our unsecured term loan and upsized the loan amount to $850 million. The loan bears interest at SOFR plus 1.20% and matures in February 2031 (as fully extended). The loan replaced the previous $800 million term loan which bore interest at SOFR plus 1.25% and was scheduled to mature in December 2027.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In February 2026, we completed a $525 million refinancing of One Park Avenue, a 945,000 square foot Manhattan office building. The five-year interest-only loan matures in February 2031 and bears interest at a rate of SOFR plus 1.78%. The loan replaced the previous $525&#160;million loan that bore interest at SOFR plus 1.22% and was scheduled to mature in March 2026.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In February 2026, a joint venture, in which we have a 45.1% interest, entered into a seven-month extension with the lenders on the $167.5&#160;million mortgage loan encumbering 61 Ninth Avenue and simultaneously paid down the principal balance by $12.5&#160;million to $155&#160;million. The loan was previously scheduled to mature in January 2026. The non-recourse, interest-only loan bears interest at a rate of SOFR plus 2.45% and matures in August 2026, with a three-month extension option subject to certain conditions. We have executed   a term sheet with the lenders to extend the loan to August 2028, with one nine-month extension.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In March 2026, the $400 million mortgage loan secured by 350 Park Avenue was defeased in connection with the development of the 350 Park Avenue site.</font></div><div style="margin-top:24pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Retail JV Preferred Equity</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In January 2025, a portion of our $1.8 billion Retail JV preferred equity was redeemed for cash of $342 million from the UNIQLO sale and, in April 2025, $407 million was redeemed for cash from the 1535 Broadway financing, </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">bringing the preferred equity balance currently to under $1.1 billion</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">.</font></div><div style="margin-top:24pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Farley, PENN 1, PENN 2 are Debt-Free</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Several years ago, when we began active development in THE </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">PENN</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New development and construction costs</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. We didn&#8217;t know then how prescient that would be. So, Farley&#47;Meta, PENN 1, and PENN 2 are now finished and paid for. These three assets, aggregating 5.2 million square feet, are  </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">free and clear and unencumbered by debt</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8230; and that&#8217;s quite a feat.</font></div><div The City That Never Sleeps</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">We believe in New York, our hometown, the most important city in America. </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">New York is the economic and cultural capital of the United States (there is a reason the Statue of Liberty is in New York Harbor)&#59; it is the finance center of the world&#59; it attracts the best and the brightest&#59; it has a large and growing highly educated and diverse workforce, eight professional sports teams, Lincoln Center and Carnegie Hall, Broadway, great museums, great restaurants and nightlife, the best hospitals and universities, and, of course, the largest concentration of Fortune 500 headquarters, and New York is now the second most important tech center in the country&#8230; you get the picture.</font></div><div style="margin-top:24pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">New York Class A Better Buildings Are In A Landlord&#8217;s Market</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Of the total 416 million square feet in Manhattan, 236 million square feet are old, tired, obsolete, and well past their sell-by date. In the </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">much smaller Class A Better Building market of 180 million square feet in which we compete</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">, availability is 7.9% for Midtown versus 18.2% in the not class A building market, with that availability evaporating quickly. Add to that, that the cost of a new build tower in New York has just about doubled over the last six to seven years, and with cost of debt of say 5.5% to 6.5%, new supply is frozen. Taken together, this all creates a </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">landlord&#8217;s market</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. We expect rents to rise aggressively, one might even say to spike... and, in fact, rents have already started to rise. So all good, very good. We at Vornado are very excited and look forward to the future. </font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">It&#8217;s a sure bet that New York</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">office will be the contrarian winner in this cycle</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Not so long ago, $100 rents were very rare. Now they are ubiquitous in the Better Buildings, with some rents reaching $200 and even  an occasional $300. Why&#63; It might be, as I have said, that there is a profound shortage of &#8220;Better&#8221; space, or it might be that the cost of  a new build has doubled (it now costs, say, $2,500 per foot to build a new tower in Manhattan). You can do the math. Even at these higher rents, it&#8217;s touch and go to make a new tower pencil. And by the way, these new builds are multi-billion-dollar monsters which are very difficult for most to finance.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Once again, in 2025, Vornado leased the most space with $100+ rents.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> See page 9.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">22</font></div></div></div><div id="ia93b0982ac5a41c886e2ca227f9cc000_73"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Development&#8230; An Internal Growth Engine</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are really good at development and have a 25-year record of great success (THE </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">PENN</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> DISTRICT, Bloomberg HQ, 220&#160;CPS,&#160;etc.,&#160;etc.). Our portfolio contains the following development projects. Note that the land sites for all these are already on balance sheet and paid for.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">350 Park Avenue, with Citadel as our anchor tenant and Ken Griffin as our 60% partner, where construction has just begun   to create a grand Norman Foster-designed 1.9 million square foot HQ tower on the best site on Park Avenue&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">PENN 15 (formerly Hotel Pennsylvania), the prime 80,000 square foot </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">PENN</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> DISTRICT land site on Seventh Avenue. This site is directly across from Madison Square Garden, is a block away from Macy&#8217;s, and is in the middle of the       Penn&#160;Station&#47;NYC subway transportation complex&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">265 West 34th Street (northeast corner of Eighth Avenue) in THE </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">PENN</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> DISTRICT, where we will shortly begin development of a 475-unit rental residential building&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">A residential tower at our 50%-owned Independence Plaza in Tribeca where our next-door neighbors are the world headquarters of both Citigroup and Goldman&#160;Sachs&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">623 Fifth Avenue, a 383,000 square foot asset that was originally built to the highest standards by Swiss Bank Corporation   as their U.S. Headquarters. Our asset sits on top of the Saks Fifth Avenue flagship and starts at Floor 11 up to Floor 36. We acquired the property in September for $218 million, $569 per square foot. Here&#8217;s why I think this is the best deal ever&#8230;</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Courier New',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">o</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.2pt">The location is in the middle of everything with unique light and air and city views. You can reach out and touch Rockefeller Center, St. Patrick&#8217;s Cathedral, JPMorganChase&#8217;s new headquarters, and even our 350 Park Avenue. Just for the fun of it, take a look at this location on Google Maps.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Courier New',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">o</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.2pt">The building is substantially vacant, which is a huge advantage to us as a developer.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Courier New',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">o</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.2pt">Built in 1990, the building is modern. Our business plan is to create here the 220 Central Park South of boutique office, i.e., the best of the best.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Courier New',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">o</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.2pt">We acquired this asset for $569 a foot. The finished product, all-in (soup to nuts, including tenant concessions) is budgeted at $1,175 a foot. We will be creating here a new building, every bit equal to a ground up new build, for half the price, in a premium platinum location.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Courier New',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">o</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.2pt">And we will deliver to tenants by the end of 2027, half the time of a new build.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Courier New',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">o</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.2pt">Recognizing that Saks Fifth Avenue, now in bankruptcy, has an uncertain future, I believe that any outcome there will be good for us.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:72pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Courier New',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">o</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.2pt">And the punchline is, at a 10.1% return on cost, with say a 5% exit or measure of value, we will achieve a double or, with leverage, a four-bagger. I expect this project to yield a $0.11 incremental increase to earnings.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">3 East 54th Street, a Plaza District development site between&#160;Fifth Avenue&#160;and&#160;Madison Avenue&#160;on 54th&#160;Street, adjacent to the&#160;St.&#160;Regis&#160;Hotel&#160;and our prime&#160;Upper Fifth Avenue&#160;retail properties. In January 2026, we acquired the asset for $141&#160;million. We previously acquired the $85 million mortgage on this property, which accreted to $107 million and was credited towards the purchase price. The site is currently zoned for 232,500 square feet as-of-right, and the location is excellent for office, hotel and&#47;or residential uses.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">We will replace the &#8220;junky&#8221; retail on 34</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">th</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Street and Seventh Avenue with modern retail offerings and greatly expanded  third-party signage.</font></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:right"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">23</font></div></div></div><div id="ia93b0982ac5a41c886e2ca227f9cc000_76"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">It Takes a Village</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Amenities, Amenities, and More Amenities</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The market is demanding </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">highest quality, heavily amenitized, transportation-based space</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. Our portfolio fits the bill&#58; THE&#160;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">PENN</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;DISTRICT (Farley, PENN 1, PENN 2, PENN 11), 1290 Avenue of the Americas, 280 Park Avenue, 555 California Street, THE&#160;MART, development sites 350 Park Avenue, 623 Fifth Avenue and PENN 15, to name a few.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">It takes a village (read, scale really matters). We believe there is a competitive advantage to owning clusters of buildings (&#224; la THE&#160;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">PENN</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;DISTRICT, Rockefeller&#160;Center, Hudson Yards). Think about it &#8211; if you&#8217;re a 300,000 or 400,000 square foot occupier in a standalone million&#160;square&#160;foot building who needs to expand by, say, 100,000 square feet, the likelihood that that would be available in your building is low. On the other hand, in our </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">PENN</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;DISTRICT village, we will certainly be able to satisfy the requirement, either in your building or an adjacent building.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are in the hospitality business, treating our tenants as guests&#59; and our guests require amenities and amenities at scale. Let&#8217;s look at  our amenity strategy. An owner can economically devote no more than two percent of building size to amenities. Even in a one million square foot standalone building, that&#8217;s only 20,000 square feet (a gym and not much else). But in THE </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">PENN</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> DISTRICT, with its 5-10 million square feet, that&#8217;s up to 200,000 square feet of amenities. What a difference.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our favorite amenities are now rooftop pavilions, social stairs, pre-function rooms, space to gather and just chill and hang, conferencing, gyms, pickleball, even a little coworking, and giant screen TVs to watch March Madness. And of course, food and restaurants aplenty.</font></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Some Thoughts, 2025 Version</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As I reread last year&#8217;s (2024) letter, much of the material is still relevant and timely and accordingly some is reprinted here.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:18pt;margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Our great nation is about to celebrate its 250</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">th</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"> birthday. How lucky are we to be Americans, living and working in the greatest country on earth!</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Does NAV Matter&#63;</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are covered by 14 analysts who estimate our NAV at $47.73 per share, with a target price of $34.50. We chronically trade at a discount to NAV. This is unacceptable and we will have to do something about it.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">AI</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">It&#8217;s always something. E-commerce was predicted to decimate physical retailing&#8230; &#8220;the malls are dead.&#8221; Then, COVID and              work-from-home (who wants to be alone all day, all night at the kitchen table&#63;) were certain to decimate office (and our cities). Now comes AI. If history is a guide, there have been four industrial revolutions, each propelling mankind to greater heights. AI is the fifth industrial revolution, which in the long run will do the same.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(8)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> In any event, just for kicks, one of my senior financial guys asked ChatGPT to predict AI&#8217;s anticipated impact on New York City office leasing. Here&#8217;s the answer&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">AI is likely to reshape New York City&#8217;s office leasing market by both reducing overall space needs and intensifying demand for high-quality assets. Productivity gains and automation&#8212;particularly in administrative, legal, and certain technical functions&#8212;will continue to drive space efficiency, limiting aggregate demand growth. However, AI is also fueling expansion in technology and data-driven sectors that still value a New York presence for talent, collaboration, and client access. These tenants are disproportionately drawn to modern, amenity-rich buildings, reinforcing the ongoing bifurcation between        top-tier assets and older, undifferentiated inventory.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">At the same time, AI is changing how office space is used and leased. As routine individual work becomes more automated, the office is increasingly a hub for collaboration, creativity, and culture&#8212;supporting demand for well-located, highly experiential environments. Leasing decisions are also becoming more data-driven, with tenants prioritizing flexibility, efficiency, and buildings that can support advanced digital infrastructure. The result is not the elimination of office demand  in New York, but a more selective, dynamic market where quality, adaptability, and technological readiness determine   leasing performance.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">I observe that this office cycle is a bit strange and really very different. </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">New York is growing and thriving</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> but most other cities are struggling with soft or no demand.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(9)</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">One theme we do think will continue is a heightened focus on the </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">quality of the landlord</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. Many landlords, particularly private ones,   are struggling with high leverage, which may limit their ability to invest capital in their buildings or, in some cases, even retain their assets. Tenants and their brokers will shun these buildings. Strong, well capitalized landlords like Vornado will benefit.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In the history of New York real estate, </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">all great landlord bull markets</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> followed a period of constrained supply, and here we are. </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Replacement cost</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> for New York office buildings is rising aggressively. It now costs at least $2,500 per foot to build a new tower in Manhattan. Replacement cost has always been a leading indicator, foretelling that the existing stock of office buildings will be increasing in value.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">It goes without saying but I must say it again, there are </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">no sacred cows in our portfolio</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. That statement includes assets such as THE&#160;MART, 555 California Street, and even some of our New York office assets, and even our retail.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are clear-eyed and realistic about the near-term financing market challenges. It is not pretty when 3% debt rolls over to 5.5%, or  even up to 6.5%. We will certainly have a few workouts to deal with over the next couple of years, but that goes with the territory. Lenders and borrowers are now playing patty cake, extending a bad loan for a couple of years and&#47;or A&#47;B structures that really accomplish nothing. The big fix and endgame for overleveraged properties is yet to come.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></div><div style="padding-left:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:4.22pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.27pt;vertical-align:baseline">8</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;There may be a dark side to AI. Some pundits are predicting 30% unemployment in white collar workers and a similar apocalypse for factory workers from robotics                                 </font></div><div style="padding-left:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">          and similar technology. That level of unemployment would hollow out our cities, cause civil insurrection, and fiscal chaos. Never gonna happen.</font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:4.22pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.27pt;vertical-align:baseline">9</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Sorry to be talking my book but San Francisco, where we own 555 California Street &#8211; the single best building, is a rapidly improving market.</font></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:right"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">27</font></div></div></div><div id="ia93b0982ac5a41c886e2ca227f9cc000_88"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:12pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Dividends</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">We continue to be rigorous with cash management.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> For 2025, we again paid a single $0.74 per share dividend in December of $154&#160;million in cash. We expect to carry over to next year this same dividend policy of a single dividend payable at year-end based   upon known facts, actual taxable income, including asset sales, etc. This strategy has been understood and endorsed by our shareholders.          I do expect that as conditions normalize, so will our dividend.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">A few facts for context&#58; In 2022, our dividend was $2.12 per share, or $435 million, in cash. Over the ten years prior to 2022, we paid $5.2&#160;billion in dividends, not including $596 million in special dividends and another $6 billion in spin-off dividends. An analyst characterized REIT dividends as sacred, and I agree&#8230; well, I sort of agree.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Buybacks</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As most of you know, I have resisted </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">buybacks</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> for years and years, resisted copy-catting and resisted the pounding from analysts to &#8220;close the NAV gap.&#8221; I believe my resistance was logical and fact-based and proven correct by the market. In April 2023, when our  stock sold off into the teens, seeing a unique opportunity, our Board authorized a $200 million share buyback program (a toe in the water). To date, we have repurchased 6,332,568 common shares at $25.67 per share.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(10)</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are pretty good at math, and it is clear to us that </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">there is a</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">huge disconnect between our stock price and the value of our assets</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. But, as a believer in the predictive power of the stock market, I am certainly aware of the recent decline of our stock and, in fact, the decline of all real estate stocks. In our case, the decline has been in the face of the best fundamentals in Manhattan in the last 20 years. Does the stock market know something or is this a once-in-a-generation buying opportunity&#63; I believe the latter. In any event, there are few investments we can find that are more attractive right now than our stock. If this disconnect continues, we will become more aggressive.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">220 Central Park South</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">After years of proudly commanding a full page and hero picture in this letter, </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">220 Central Park South</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">, basically completed, now gets this short paragraph. Sales to date have totaled $3.308 billion. We are 99% sold with, I guesstimate, $15 million still to come from one remaining unit. As an indicator of the singular success of this product, resale prices are up, and up substantially, and I believe 220 to be the only recent development where resale prices have increased. </font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">With 220 CPS, we are the undisputed heavyweight champion. We have the dominant franchise in luxury condominiums and get frequent calls to participate in new projects. There are now half a dozen new condo projects either started or about to start within a three-block radius of 57</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">th</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Street and Fifth Avenue, the center of the Plaza District. I am wary.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Here&#8217;s the Alexander&#8217;s Story</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Vornado owns 32.4% of Alexander&#8217;s, Inc. common stock. I am Chairman and CEO. Here&#8217;s the recent activity&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">In May 2023, we sold the Rego Park Z land parcel in Queens for $71 million.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">In May 2024, we extended to 2040 the million-foot Bloomberg lease which was set to expire in 2029&#59; thus giving us 15 years of lease term.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">We refinanced the $500 million of debt on the Bloomberg asset which was set to expire in 2024. We paid the new four-year loan down to $400 million&#59; importantly, the loan is freely prepayable.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">In December 2025, we recapitalized the $300 million grossly overleveraged 731 Lexington Avenue retail condominium. See page 10 for details. We expect the reletting of that retail space will create value approximately equal to the $132.5 million   we paid for the A-Note plus related capital of give-or-take $50 million.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">Recognizing that the Rego Park I land site in the middle of Queens is much more valuable than the half-empty 60-year-old antique shopping center, we vacated the site by relocating its tenants to Rego Park II and have contracted to sell the site to Northwell Health for $202 million.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">Rego Park II is now a strong, well-leased</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(11)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> 600,000 square foot thriving urban property.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">Our dividend policy at Alexander&#8217;s has been to pay a regular $18 per share &#8211; in effect through thick and thin, $18 being our calculation of the long-term earning power of the assets. What would be served by cutting the dividend, starving shareholders, just to increase the cash balance of an already cash-rich balance sheet&#63;</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;padding-left:36pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:15.2pt">So&#8230; after all this activity, Alexander&#8217;s is now the Bloomberg HQ on a 15-year lease, the 731 Lexington retail lease-up, the 600,000 fully-leased</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(11)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Rego II thriving urban shopping center, with modest debt and large cash balances&#59; pretty simple and easy to underwrite.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:4.22pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.27pt;vertical-align:baseline">10</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Think about this&#8230; Vornado stock is a better buy today than it was at $15 three years ago.</font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:4.22pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.27pt;vertical-align:baseline">11</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One last large space is in lease.</font></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">28</font></div></div></div><div id="ia93b0982ac5a41c886e2ca227f9cc000_91"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:12pt"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">JBG SMITH</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">JBG SMITH was born in 2017, nine years ago, in a spin-merge transaction with Vornado spinning our Washington, DC office business (acquired from Bob Smith and Bob Kogod in 2002) and simultaneously merging with local sharpshooter JBG. JBG was the only Washington player who really believed in Crystal City, our large office and apartment complex on the shores of the Potomac River.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">JBG&#8217;s Matt Kelly</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(12) </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">was CEO and I was founding Chairman.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(13)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> The business plan was to raze the 50-year-old buildings</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(14)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> to develop apartments, taking advantage of zoning which we had just completed to allow for one and a half times rebuild for a teardown.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">CEO Matt Kelly has done a fine job with kudos for Amazon HQ2, selling $1.3 billion of old office buildings, building 3,350 new apartment units, and for buying back 63% of the shares at $18.77. </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">So&#8230; it seems that</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">what was a buyback program has now become    a tontine.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">What&#8217;s going on here&#63; And nobody seems to care.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> The federal debt is now $38 trillion, a $10 trillion increase from just five years     ago. What&#8217;s more &#8211; annual deficits are running close to $2 trillion and the national debt is projected to be $47 trillion by 2030.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(15)(16)</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Many of our cities and states are no better. The heavily populated northern, blue cities &#8211; what I call the northern crown of America &#8211; Washington, Philadelphia, New York, Chicago, Seattle, Portland, San Francisco, and Los Angeles are all indulging runaway budgets     and increasing taxes.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">There is a natural competition between </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">high-tax</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">, densely populated urban centers and </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">low-tax&#47;no-tax</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">, generally warm weather, business welcoming states. Take a hard look at these numbers&#58;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New department, the first governor of a northern, densely populated, urban state who recognizes      all this and reduces expenses and taxes will be lionized.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">I again question the wisdom of the </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">New York State estate tax</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">. I repeat here what I have said before. In New York State, the top 2%     pay a full 50% of personal income taxes so it is critical that they remain tax-paying residents. The vulnerability comes with the 2%-ers, who are at the end of their careers. Most of the folks I know are willing to pay higher income taxes for the privilege of living in New&#160;York but hate the prospect of a 16% toll for the privilege of dying in New York. New York State&#8217;s estate tax brings in approximately one half  of one percent of the state&#8217;s annual budget. </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">The estate tax should be repealed.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Keeping our highest taxpayers through the end of their lives is both good economic policy and good politics. By the way, high-tax California has no estate tax, and New Jersey repealed its   estate tax in 2018. But nobody is listening and that&#8217;s a shame.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Here&#8217;s an idea for the powers that be&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">repeal the scaffold law</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> which will save 5% on every construction project (public or private) in     the state. New York is the only state in the nation with such a law and, as a result, New York&#8217;s insurance costs 8% vs. 3% in New Jersey. This should be an easy one.</font></div><div style="margin-top:18pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Sustainability</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our board and senior management are proud of Vornado&#8217;s continued national leadership in sustainability. See the extensive material in  the Sustainability section of our website, which can be found at </font><font style="color:#0e32e1;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">www.vno.com&#47;sustainability</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">.</font></div><div style="margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:4.22pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.27pt;vertical-align:baseline">12</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A Dartmouth man.</font></div><div style="padding-left:9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:4.22pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.27pt;vertical-align:baseline">13</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;It could be said that I was the father of JBG SMITH.
